bull_bear.body:
- "Completed Rs 900 crore QIP in June 2025, with Rs 340 crores earmarked for debt reduction" and "Achieved net cash position post-QIP, significantly strengthening balance sheet".
- Net debt chart shows Rs 838 Cr (FY23), Rs 751 Cr (FY24), Rs 542 Cr (FY25) and nil for both FY26 and FY27 Q1; the debt profile is described as "a conservative financial approach with a strong focus on maintaining low leverage, optimizing cost of capital, and ensuring ample liquidity".
- ~Rs 200+ Cr of acquisition capital is stated as available, with liquidity giving "the flexibility to pursue growth opportunities, accelerate project execution and enhance shareholder value".
- Expected surplus from ongoing projects is Rs 958 Cr on a 100% share basis and Rs 727 Cr on MNRL's share, against a cost to complete of Rs 1,461 Cr (100%) / Rs 928 Cr (MNRL share); OC-ready inventory adds Rs 247 Cr of surplus on MNRL's share.
- Growth has been acquisition-led: the milestone timeline lists purchases of Piramal Spinning & Weaving Mills (8 acres), 5.85 acres in Bhandup, 12.2 acres of Khatau Mills in Byculla, a JV stake in Futurex, Sanvo Resorts (25 acres in Panvel), Terrapolis Assets (1 acre in Mulund), Nexzone Fiscal Services (14 acres in Bhandup), controlling stakes in 3 real estate entities adding ~Rs 840 Cr of GDV potential, and a 90% stake in Sunset Spaces Pvt Ltd to strengthen the redevelopment pipeline.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Self-described as a "Leading Mumbai-focused real estate developer with a diversified presence across key micro-markets", with ongoing projects at Panvel, Byculla, Lower Parel, Bhandup and Mulund.
- Growth is framed around six stated drivers: Amalgamation & Arrangement, strategically positioned land banks and dominance in key micro markets, strong liquidity, diversified portfolio for risk mitigation, and excellent in-house capabilities.
- Marathon Group (not the listed entity) credentials cited: established in 1978, 55+ years of experience, 100+ projects delivered, 10,000+ families housed, 15,000+ homes in the pipeline and 4 Mn sq.ft. of land under development.
- Monte South, Byculla is claimed to be "Among the top 5 projects in Byculla market by marketable supply", with 7.8 lakh sq. ft. (~Rs 2,403 Cr) sold to date.
- MNRL's own origin is stated as 2002 with the acquisition of Piramal Spinning & Weaving Mills Ltd (holding 8 acres of land) through the BIFR, rebranded as Marathon Nextgen Realty Limited in 2007.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Amalgamation] A scheme of Amalgamation & Arrangement would consolidate promoter and promoter-group assets into MNRL (the listed company); it has "Received 'No Adverse Observations' from BSE & NSE; Scheme now awaits NCLT approval" — i.e. it is not yet effective.
- [Merger impact on scale] Portfolio GDV moves from a pre-merger sub-total of Rs 18,792 Cr (unsold Rs 12,013 Cr; MNRL share of unsold Rs 7,606 Cr) to a post-merger total of Rs 20,751 Cr (unsold Rs 13,483 Cr; MNRL share of unsold Rs 8,723 Cr), with Futurex 2 (Rs 1,059 Cr) and Nextown (Rs 900 Cr) added.
- [Reporting basis] The deck reports Q1 FY27 operations on two bases in parallel — "Existing Portfolio" and "Merged Portfolio" — and states results are "Based on 40% share for Monte South project", with financial highlights noting inclusion of "actual sales value attributable to capital gains on FutureX inventory and 40% of Monte South turnover".
- [Partial ownership] Several assets are held below 100%: Monte South at 40%, Kanjurmarg acquisitions at 34% economic interest, Nexzone at 91%, NeoValley at 90%, Nextown at 59% and Marathon Ener-Gen LLP at 59.3%, so headline GDV and area figures diverge materially from MNRL's share.
- [Leadership] Promoter-family led: Chairman Chetan R. Shah (IIT Bombay, 40+ years), Vice Chairman Mayur R. Shah (30+ years, former President of MCHI-CREDAI), with next-generation directors heading specific projects (Nexzone/Futurex, Nexworld).

themes.title: Real-estate up-cycle - premium housing & redevelopment
themes.need: The residential up-cycle is now presales-led with a visible margin cost. SOBHA posted its highest-ever presales at INR 3,656cr (+76% YoY, 2.34 msf at an average INR 15,655/sqft, NCR at a record INR 1,384cr) and guided FY27 presales at +30% or better - but reported EBITDA is still only ~9.7%, guided to 17-20% only by exit-Q4, and forthcoming-project marginal cash flow was cut from ~INR 86bn to INR 68.3bn on a heavier joint-development mix. SUNTECK booked INR 787cr of presales (+20%) with ZERO launches in the quarter, with aspirational-luxury (Naigaon/Kalyan) at 21% of presales 'picking up because of the lower interest rate' - the first sign the rate-elastic end is turning on demand rather than inventory release. DLF's FY26 bookings of INR20,143cr and 50mn sq ft of rental at 95% occupancy anchor the annuity leg; LODHA/GODREJPROP/PRESTIGE-tier and MMR redevelopers (RUSTOMJEE, KALPATARU, RAYMONDREL, MANINFRA, SURAJEST) ride premiumization; PHOENIXLTD/EMBDL on mixed-use.
themes.driver: SOBHA's exit-Q4 margin ramp from ~9.7% to 17-20% is the falsifiable claim (JD-heavy growth structurally lowers marginal margins); rate-elastic aspirational absorption (SUNTECK); FY27 launch-pipeline execution and festive booking momentum.
